- Pedir ao mesmo agente que avalie o próprio trabalho — Builder ≠ Evaluator.
- Implementar UI nova sem passar por `harness-frontend-builder` (perde Gemini Pro).

- `.harness/MODELS.md` — tabela de modelos e effort matrix.
- `.harness/harness.config.yaml` — single source of truth de routing.

# Claude Code Multi-Agent Harness: What Actually Works in Production

## Executive Summary

The official Claude Code documentation is authoritative and detailed. Most of the architecture used in the Gidape harness is sound and aligns with official patterns — but several specific claims in CLAUDE.md and common community practice diverge from how the system actually works. This report distinguishes **official Anthropic documentation** (from `code.claude.com/docs`), **Anthropic engineering posts** (from `anthropic.com/engineering`), and **community practice** at every claim.

---

## 1. Native `.claude/agents/` Subagent Files

**Status: Fully documented and supported — official Anthropic docs.**

Source: [Create custom subagents — code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)

### How it works

- Subagent definitions are **Markdown files with YAML frontmatter** stored in `.claude/agents/` (project scope) or `~/.claude/agents/` (user scope).
- Each file has two required fields: `name` and `description`. Everything else is optional.
- The `description` is what Claude uses to decide **when to automatically delegate**. The better the description, the more reliably Claude routes to that subagent.
- Each subagent runs in **its own context window** with a custom system prompt — not the full Claude Code system prompt.
- Subagents inherit CLAUDE.md files from the main session (exception: built-in `Explore` and `Plan` subagents skip CLAUDE.md for speed).

### Complete supported frontmatter fields (official)

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | Lowercase + hyphens; this is what `agent_type` resolves to in hooks |
| `description` | Yes | What Claude reads to decide when to delegate |
| `tools` | No | Allowlist; inherits all tools if omitted |
| `disallowedTools` | No | Denylist applied before `tools` allowlist |
| `model` | No | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, full model ID (e.g. `claude-opus-4-8`), or `inherit` (default) |
| `permissionMode` | No | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan` |
| `maxTurns` | No | Hard cap on agentic turns |
| `skills` | No | Skills preloaded into context at startup |
| `mcpServers` | No | MCP servers scoped to this subagent only |
| `hooks` | No | Lifecycle hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) |
| `memory` | No | `user`, `project`, or `local` for cross-session persistent memory |
| `background` | No | `true` = always run as background task |
| `effort` | No | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| `isolation` | No | `worktree` = isolated git worktree for this subagent |
| `color` | No | Display color in task list |
| `initialPrompt` | No | Auto-submitted first user turn when agent runs as main session via `--agent` |

### Critical constraint: subagents cannot spawn other subagents

> "Subagents cannot spawn other subagents. If your workflow requires nested delegation, use Skills or chain subagents from the main conversation." — official docs

This is a hard architectural limit. The `Agent` tool is **not available inside subagent context**. Any harness design that relies on subagents spawning further subagents will silently fail.

### `subagent_type` parameter

The term `subagent_type` appears in hooks context, not as an invocation parameter. Specifically: `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` hooks receive the agent's `name` field value as the `agent_type` matcher input. When using `--agents` CLI JSON, you reference agents by key name. When using `Agent(agent_type)` syntax in tools allowlist, the parenthesized value is the agent's `name`.

**Note on tool rename:** As of Claude Code v2.1.63, the `Task` tool was renamed to `Agent`. `Task(...)` references in existing configurations still work as aliases.

---

## 2. Slash Commands (`.claude/commands/`)

**Status: Supported but officially deprecated in favor of `.claude/skills/`. Both work.**

Source: [Slash Commands in the SDK — code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/slash-commands](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/slash-commands), [Best practices — code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

### What they are

- Markdown files in `.claude/commands/` (project) or `~/.claude/commands/` (user).
- The filename (without `.md`) becomes the slash command: `review.md` → `/review`.
- Optional YAML frontmatter supports: `description`, `allowed-tools`, `model`, `argument-hint`.
- `$ARGUMENTS` (or `$0`, `$1` etc.) inserts user arguments.
- Commands can embed `!`\`bash command\`` to run live shell output at invocation time.
- Can reference file contents with `@path/to/file`.

### Do slash commands trigger multi-agent pipelines?

**No directly, but yes indirectly.** A slash command is a prompt template — it runs in the main conversation context. It can instruct Claude to "use the security-reviewer subagent to…" and Claude will then invoke the Agent tool to spawn the subagent. The command itself does not mechanically spawn agents; it issues instructions that Claude then executes, including delegating to subagents.

The recommended modern replacement is `.claude/skills/` with `SKILL.md` files. Skills support the same `/name` invocation plus **autonomous invocation** (Claude can load them without being explicitly told to). The CLI continues to support both formats.

---

## 3. CLAUDE.md: Documented Limitations and Recommended Size

**Status: Officially documented with explicit warnings about length.**

Source: [Best practices — code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

### The official guidance (verbatim)

> "Keep it concise. For each line, ask: 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?' If not, cut it. **Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!**"

> "CLAUDE.md is loaded every session, so only include things that apply broadly."

> Recommended: **under 200 lines, under 2,000 tokens.**

> "The most important resource to manage [is] Claude's context window. LLM performance degrades as context fills."

### What causes CLAUDE.md instructions to be ignored

The best-practices docs explicitly call out the failure mode: a CLAUDE.md that is too long causes important rules to get lost in noise. The failure pattern is named: **"The over-specified CLAUDE.md"** — if Claude keeps violating a rule, the fix is to ruthlessly prune the file, not add more.

### CLAUDE.md can import other files

Via `@path/to/file` syntax — this is the correct pattern for large contextual documents. Reference them from a concise CLAUDE.md rather than inlining everything.

### What CLAUDE.md does NOT do

- It is **advisory**, not deterministic. Rules can be missed.
- For deterministic enforcement, use **hooks** (scripts that run at lifecycle events, cannot be ignored).
- CLAUDE.md files are loaded into every subagent's context too (except built-in Explore and Plan).

### Implication for the Gidape harness

The current `CLAUDE.md` is far over the recommended 200-line / 2,000-token threshold. This is a documented cause of instruction-following degradation. The `@path/to/import` mechanism should be used to split content into imported files, keeping the root CLAUDE.md under the threshold.

---

## 4. Orchestrator Pattern: Claude Code Sessions vs. API

**Status: The orchestrator-calls-subagents pattern is natively supported in Claude Code sessions via the Agent tool.**

Sources: [code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents), [code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams), [anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)

### Two separate systems

**System A — Subagents (within a single session):**
- One Claude instance (the main conversation) uses the **Agent tool** to spawn subagents.
- Each subagent has its own context window and returns only a summary to the main context.
- Subagents are defined in `.claude/agents/` files OR created ad-hoc by Claude.
- Subagents **cannot spawn further subagents** — depth is fixed at 1.
- This is stable and available in all Claude Code versions.

**System B — Agent Teams (multiple coordinated sessions, experimental):**
- Requires `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` in settings.
- Requires Claude Code v2.1.32+.
- A team lead creates teammates — separate Claude Code instances — with a shared task list and mailbox.
- Teammates can communicate directly with each other, not just back to the lead.
- Teammates **cannot spawn their own teams** (no nesting).
- Marked explicitly as experimental with known limitations: no session resumption with in-process teammates, task status can lag, one team at a time.

### Anthropic's Multi-Agent Research System

Source: [anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)

This is Anthropic's internal research tool. Key verified facts:
- Uses **Claude Opus 4** as lead agent, **Claude Sonnet 4** as subagents. This mix outperformed single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2%.
- The document does **not specify** whether it runs on the Messages API directly or via Claude Code sessions — the implementation details are not disclosed.
- The pattern described (lead agent decomposes task → spawns parallel specialist subagents → synthesizes) is the same pattern that `.claude/agents/` + the Agent tool implements in Claude Code.
- Key production lessons: error handling with checkpoints, observability without reading contents, rainbow deployments, external memory for long research, routing subagent output to filesystem instead of funneling through lead context.

**Conclusion:** The orchestrator pattern applies to both API-level multi-agent systems and Claude Code sessions. The Claude Code Agent tool is the mechanism for Claude Code sessions.

---

## 5. Subagents vs. Agent Teams: The Practical Difference

**Status: Officially documented with a comparison table.**

Source: [code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams)

| | Subagents | Agent Teams |
|---|---|---|
| Context | Own context; results return to main | Own context; fully independent |
| Communication | Report results to main agent only | Teammates message each other directly |
| Coordination | Main agent manages all work | Shared task list + self-coordination |
| Best for | Focused tasks where only result matters | Complex work requiring discussion |
| Token cost | Lower (results summarized back) | Higher (each is a separate Claude instance) |
| Stability | Stable | Experimental, with known limitations |
| Subagent nesting | No | No (teammates cannot spawn teams) |

**The critical difference:** subagents in `.claude/agents/` can be referenced by agent teams when spawning teammates, giving you the ability to define a role once and use it in both patterns.

---

## 6. Slash Commands vs. Skills: The Current State

**Status: Skills (`.claude/skills/`) are the current recommended format; commands (`.claude/commands/`) are legacy but still supported.**

Source: [code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

Skills (`SKILL.md` files) support:
- Same `/name` slash invocation as commands
- **Autonomous invocation** — Claude can load and apply them without being explicitly told, based on relevance
- `disable-model-invocation: true` for workflows that should only run when explicitly triggered
- Can specify `context: fork` to run skill in a forked subagent

Slash commands (`.claude/commands/`) are listed as legacy. The CLI supports both. There is no migration urgency, but new harnesses should use Skills.

---

## 7. Is CLAUDE.md Orchestration Architecturally Correct?

**Status: Partially correct by design, but structurally limited.**

### What works

Using CLAUDE.md to define orchestration behavior (which subagents to invoke, when, in what sequence) is a **supported pattern** according to official docs. CLAUDE.md is read by the main session and by subagents (except Explore/Plan). Orchestration instructions in CLAUDE.md are advisory — Claude reads them and acts on them via the Agent tool.

### What does NOT work (hard constraints)

1. **Subagents spawning subagents**: impossible. If your CLAUDE.md instructs a subagent to "call harness-evaluator after harness-builder finishes," the subagent cannot do this — the Agent tool is unavailable inside subagent context. Only the main session can spawn subagents.

2. **CLAUDE.md length causing instruction loss**: at the documented threshold (~2,000 tokens), instructions become unreliable. A complex pipeline defined entirely in CLAUDE.md will experience degraded adherence.

3. **CLAUDE.md is not deterministic**: instructions can be missed or deprioritized. For guaranteed execution (lint before commit, security check on migration files), use hooks in `.claude/settings.json`.

### What is the correct architecture

The correct multi-layer approach is:

- **CLAUDE.md** (concise, <2000 tokens): project conventions, naming, absolute rules. Use `@path/to/file` imports for detailed docs.
- **`.claude/agents/`**: define specialized subagents with precise descriptions so Claude knows when to delegate automatically or on request.
- **`.claude/settings.json` hooks**: for deterministic lifecycle enforcement (SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop).
- **Skills** (`.claude/skills/`): reusable prompts/workflows invokable as slash commands or autonomously.
- **CLAUDE.md orchestration routing**: acceptable for soft routing guidance, not for hard pipeline enforcement.

---

## 8. Real-World Harness Examples (Community Practice)

**Status: Multiple public examples exist; quality varies widely.**

Sources: [github.com/wshobson/agents](https://github.com/wshobson/agents), [github.com/aws-samples/sample-claude-code-agent-team](https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-claude-code-agent-team), [github.com/revfactory/claude-code-harness](https://github.com/revfactory/claude-code-harness), [github.com/ruvnet/ruflo](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo)

### AWS Sample (most authoritative non-Anthropic source)

`aws-samples/sample-claude-code-agent-team`: Full Stack Developer parent orchestrating three specialists: Coding Agent, DevOps Agent, Review Agent. Uses spec-driven development, native agent teams feature.

### wshobson/agents (community marketplace)

84 plugins, 192 agents, 156 skills, 102 commands all defined as Markdown files. Cross-compatible with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI. Uses the native `.claude/agents/` format.

### revfactory/harness (A/B tested)

Framework using architectural blueprints + role-based agent definitions + workflow orchestration via CLAUDE.md. Reported 60% quality improvement (49.5 → 79.3/100) in controlled experiment across 15 SE tasks. Uses CLAUDE.md as the primary orchestration layer.

### Anthropic's own blog post: dynamic workflows

Source: [claude.com/blog/a-harness-for-every-task-dynamic-workflows-in-claude-code](https://claude.com/blog/a-harness-for-every-task-dynamic-workflows-in-claude-code)

Anthropic uses the term "harness" to mean "the orchestration framework that coordinates agent execution." The key concept is **dynamic workflows** — Claude Opus 4.8+ can write its own orchestration harness (JavaScript) on the fly for each task rather than always using the static default. This is distinct from static CLAUDE.md-based orchestration. Dynamic workflows can: decide which models subagents use, run subagents in isolated worktrees, resume from checkpoints, process data programmatically.

---

## 9. Adversarial Verification: Claims That Need Correction

### Claim: "harness-builder invokes harness-evaluator"

**Partially incorrect.** If harness-builder runs as a subagent, it cannot spawn harness-evaluator (or any subagent). The main orchestrator session must invoke evaluator after builder returns. The pipeline in CLAUDE.md should direct the **orchestrator** to call both in sequence, not builder to call evaluator.

### Claim: Agent tool with `subagent_type` parameter

**Needs precision.** The `subagent_type` term appears in hooks documentation (as the value passed to `agent_type` matchers in SubagentStart/Stop hooks). When Claude invokes the Agent tool, it identifies the target subagent by its `name` field. The `--agents` CLI flag accepts a JSON object where keys are agent names. There is no separate "subagent_type" invocation parameter in the Agent tool itself — the routing is by name.

### Claim: `.claude/agents/` supports specifying provider (Claude vs. Gemini)

**Not supported via frontmatter.** The `model` field accepts model aliases and full Anthropic model IDs only (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, or `claude-*` IDs). Non-Anthropic models are not selectable via the `model` frontmatter field. Running Gemini models as subagents requires an MCP server or external tool bridge, not native frontmatter routing.

### Claim: CLAUDE.md orchestration is reliable for multi-step pipelines

**Conditionally true.** Works for soft routing if the file is concise. Fails for hard enforcement if the file is bloated. The official docs are explicit: long CLAUDE.md = ignored instructions. For a pipeline as complex as the Gidape harness, the instructions will compete with each other for attention.

---

## 10. Recommended Architecture for the Gidape Harness (Synthesis)

Based entirely on official documentation:

1. **Slim CLAUDE.md to <200 lines.** Use `@.harness/constitution.md`, `@.harness/memory-bank/product.md` etc. via import syntax. The routing table and pipeline description belong in imported files.

2. **`.claude/agents/` files for every subagent.** Currently working correctly. Descriptions are the routing mechanism — make them precise and include "use proactively when..." phrasing.

3. **Main session as orchestrator.** The orchestrator cannot be a subagent. The main Claude Code session invokes Agent tool → routes to subagents → receives summaries → chains to next agent. This matches the current design.

5. **Agent Teams for true parallelism.** When builder and evaluator need to run concurrently and communicate, Agent Teams (experimental) is the correct feature. Today's sequential delegation (builder → evaluator) is correct for the non-experimental path.

6. **Subagent cannot call subagent.** Any spec that describes "harness-builder spawns harness-evaluator" must be revised: the orchestrator must chain them.

---

# Claude Code Multi-Agent Harness: What Actually Works in Production

## Executive Summary

The official Claude Code documentation is authoritative and detailed. Most of the architecture used in the Gidape harness is sound and aligns with official patterns — but several specific claims in CLAUDE.md and common community practice diverge from how the system actually works. This report distinguishes **official Anthropic documentation** (from `code.claude.com/docs`), **Anthropic engineering posts** (from `anthropic.com/engineering`), and **community practice** at every claim.

---

## 1. Native `.claude/agents/` Subagent Files

**Status: Fully documented and supported — official Anthropic docs.**

Source: [Create custom subagents — code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)

### How it works

- Subagent definitions are **Markdown files with YAML frontmatter** stored in `.claude/agents/` (project scope) or `~/.claude/agents/` (user scope).
- Each file has two required fields: `name` and `description`. Everything else is optional.
- The `description` is what Claude uses to decide **when to automatically delegate**. The better the description, the more reliably Claude routes to that subagent.
- Each subagent runs in **its own context window** with a custom system prompt — not the full Claude Code system prompt.
- Subagents inherit CLAUDE.md files from the main session (exception: built-in `Explore` and `Plan` subagents skip CLAUDE.md for speed).

### Complete supported frontmatter fields (official)

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | Lowercase + hyphens; this is what `agent_type` resolves to in hooks |
| `description` | Yes | What Claude reads to decide when to delegate |
| `tools` | No | Allowlist; inherits all tools if omitted |
| `disallowedTools` | No | Denylist applied before `tools` allowlist |
| `model` | No | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, full model ID (e.g. `claude-opus-4-8`), or `inherit` (default) |
| `permissionMode` | No | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan` |
| `maxTurns` | No | Hard cap on agentic turns |
| `skills` | No | Skills preloaded into context at startup |
| `mcpServers` | No | MCP servers scoped to this subagent only |
| `hooks` | No | Lifecycle hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) |
| `memory` | No | `user`, `project`, or `local` for cross-session persistent memory |
| `background` | No | `true` = always run as background task |
| `effort` | No | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| `isolation` | No | `worktree` = isolated git worktree for this subagent |
| `color` | No | Display color in task list |
| `initialPrompt` | No | Auto-submitted first user turn when agent runs as main session via `--agent` |

### Critical constraint: subagents cannot spawn other subagents

> "Subagents cannot spawn other subagents. If your workflow requires nested delegation, use Skills or chain subagents from the main conversation." — official docs

This is a hard architectural limit. The `Agent` tool is **not available inside subagent context**. Any harness design that relies on subagents spawning further subagents will silently fail.

### `subagent_type` parameter

The term `subagent_type` appears in hooks context, not as an invocation parameter. Specifically: `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` hooks receive the agent's `name` field value as the `agent_type` matcher input. When using `--agents` CLI JSON, you reference agents by key name. When using `Agent(agent_type)` syntax in tools allowlist, the parenthesized value is the agent's `name`.

**Note on tool rename:** As of Claude Code v2.1.63, the `Task` tool was renamed to `Agent`. `Task(...)` references in existing configurations still work as aliases.

---

## 2. Slash Commands (`.claude/commands/`)

**Status: Supported but officially deprecated in favor of `.claude/skills/`. Both work.**

Source: [Slash Commands in the SDK — code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/slash-commands](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/slash-commands), [Best practices — code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

### What they are

- Markdown files in `.claude/commands/` (project) or `~/.claude/commands/` (user).
- The filename (without `.md`) becomes the slash command: `review.md` → `/review`.
- Optional YAML frontmatter supports: `description`, `allowed-tools`, `model`, `argument-hint`.
- `$ARGUMENTS` (or `$0`, `$1` etc.) inserts user arguments.
- Commands can embed `!`\`bash command\`` to run live shell output at invocation time.
- Can reference file contents with `@path/to/file`.

### Do slash commands trigger multi-agent pipelines?

**No directly, but yes indirectly.** A slash command is a prompt template — it runs in the main conversation context. It can instruct Claude to "use the security-reviewer subagent to…" and Claude will then invoke the Agent tool to spawn the subagent. The command itself does not mechanically spawn agents; it issues instructions that Claude then executes, including delegating to subagents.

The recommended modern replacement is `.claude/skills/` with `SKILL.md` files. Skills support the same `/name` invocation plus **autonomous invocation** (Claude can load them without being explicitly told to). The CLI continues to support both formats.

---

## 3. CLAUDE.md: Documented Limitations and Recommended Size

**Status: Officially documented with explicit warnings about length.**

Source: [Best practices — code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

### The official guidance (verbatim)

> "Keep it concise. For each line, ask: 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?' If not, cut it. **Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!**"

> "CLAUDE.md is loaded every session, so only include things that apply broadly."

> Recommended: **under 200 lines, under 2,000 tokens.**

> "The most important resource to manage [is] Claude's context window. LLM performance degrades as context fills."

### What causes CLAUDE.md instructions to be ignored

The best-practices docs explicitly call out the failure mode: a CLAUDE.md that is too long causes important rules to get lost in noise. The failure pattern is named: **"The over-specified CLAUDE.md"** — if Claude keeps violating a rule, the fix is to ruthlessly prune the file, not add more.

### CLAUDE.md can import other files

Via `@path/to/file` syntax — this is the correct pattern for large contextual documents. Reference them from a concise CLAUDE.md rather than inlining everything.

### What CLAUDE.md does NOT do

- It is **advisory**, not deterministic. Rules can be missed.
- For deterministic enforcement, use **hooks** (scripts that run at lifecycle events, cannot be ignored).
- CLAUDE.md files are loaded into every subagent's context too (except built-in Explore and Plan).

### Implication for the Gidape harness

The current `CLAUDE.md` is far over the recommended 200-line / 2,000-token threshold. This is a documented cause of instruction-following degradation. The `@path/to/import` mechanism should be used to split content into imported files, keeping the root CLAUDE.md under the threshold.

---

## 4. Orchestrator Pattern: Claude Code Sessions vs. API

**Status: The orchestrator-calls-subagents pattern is natively supported in Claude Code sessions via the Agent tool.**

Sources: [code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents), [code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams), [anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)

### Two separate systems

**System A — Subagents (within a single session):**
- One Claude instance (the main conversation) uses the **Agent tool** to spawn subagents.
- Each subagent has its own context window and returns only a summary to the main context.
- Subagents are defined in `.claude/agents/` files OR created ad-hoc by Claude.
- Subagents **cannot spawn further subagents** — depth is fixed at 1.
- This is stable and available in all Claude Code versions.

**System B — Agent Teams (multiple coordinated sessions, experimental):**
- Requires `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1` in settings.
- Requires Claude Code v2.1.32+.
- A team lead creates teammates — separate Claude Code instances — with a shared task list and mailbox.
- Teammates can communicate directly with each other, not just back to the lead.
- Teammates **cannot spawn their own teams** (no nesting).
- Marked explicitly as experimental with known limitations: no session resumption with in-process teammates, task status can lag, one team at a time.

### Anthropic's Multi-Agent Research System

Source: [anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)

This is Anthropic's internal research tool. Key verified facts:
- Uses **Claude Opus 4** as lead agent, **Claude Sonnet 4** as subagents. This mix outperformed single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2%.
- The document does **not specify** whether it runs on the Messages API directly or via Claude Code sessions — the implementation details are not disclosed.
- The pattern described (lead agent decomposes task → spawns parallel specialist subagents → synthesizes) is the same pattern that `.claude/agents/` + the Agent tool implements in Claude Code.
- Key production lessons: error handling with checkpoints, observability without reading contents, rainbow deployments, external memory for long research, routing subagent output to filesystem instead of funneling through lead context.

**Conclusion:** The orchestrator pattern applies to both API-level multi-agent systems and Claude Code sessions. The Claude Code Agent tool is the mechanism for Claude Code sessions.

---

## 5. Subagents vs. Agent Teams: The Practical Difference

**Status: Officially documented with a comparison table.**

Source: [code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams)

| | Subagents | Agent Teams |
|---|---|---|
| Context | Own context; results return to main | Own context; fully independent |
| Communication | Report results to main agent only | Teammates message each other directly |
| Coordination | Main agent manages all work | Shared task list + self-coordination |
| Best for | Focused tasks where only result matters | Complex work requiring discussion |
| Token cost | Lower (results summarized back) | Higher (each is a separate Claude instance) |
| Stability | Stable | Experimental, with known limitations |
| Subagent nesting | No | No (teammates cannot spawn teams) |

**The critical difference:** subagents in `.claude/agents/` can be referenced by agent teams when spawning teammates, giving you the ability to define a role once and use it in both patterns.

---

## 6. Slash Commands vs. Skills: The Current State

**Status: Skills (`.claude/skills/`) are the current recommended format; commands (`.claude/commands/`) are legacy but still supported.**

Source: [code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

Skills (`SKILL.md` files) support:
- Same `/name` slash invocation as commands
- **Autonomous invocation** — Claude can load and apply them without being explicitly told, based on relevance
- `disable-model-invocation: true` for workflows that should only run when explicitly triggered
- Can specify `context: fork` to run skill in a forked subagent

Slash commands (`.claude/commands/`) are listed as legacy. The CLI supports both. There is no migration urgency, but new harnesses should use Skills.

---

## 7. Is CLAUDE.md Orchestration Architecturally Correct?

**Status: Partially correct by design, but structurally limited.**

### What works

Using CLAUDE.md to define orchestration behavior (which subagents to invoke, when, in what sequence) is a **supported pattern** according to official docs. CLAUDE.md is read by the main session and by subagents (except Explore/Plan). Orchestration instructions in CLAUDE.md are advisory — Claude reads them and acts on them via the Agent tool.

### What does NOT work (hard constraints)

1. **Subagents spawning subagents**: impossible. If your CLAUDE.md instructs a subagent to "call harness-evaluator after harness-builder finishes," the subagent cannot do this — the Agent tool is unavailable inside subagent context. Only the main session can spawn subagents.

2. **CLAUDE.md length causing instruction loss**: at the documented threshold (~2,000 tokens), instructions become unreliable. A complex pipeline defined entirely in CLAUDE.md will experience degraded adherence.

3. **CLAUDE.md is not deterministic**: instructions can be missed or deprioritized. For guaranteed execution (lint before commit, security check on migration files), use hooks in `.claude/settings.json`.

### What is the correct architecture

The correct multi-layer approach is:

- **CLAUDE.md** (concise, <2000 tokens): project conventions, naming, absolute rules. Use `@path/to/file` imports for detailed docs.
- **`.claude/agents/`**: define specialized subagents with precise descriptions so Claude knows when to delegate automatically or on request.
- **`.claude/settings.json` hooks**: for deterministic lifecycle enforcement (SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop).
- **Skills** (`.claude/skills/`): reusable prompts/workflows invokable as slash commands or autonomously.
- **CLAUDE.md orchestration routing**: acceptable for soft routing guidance, not for hard pipeline enforcement.

---

## 8. Real-World Harness Examples (Community Practice)

**Status: Multiple public examples exist; quality varies widely.**

Sources: [github.com/wshobson/agents](https://github.com/wshobson/agents), [github.com/aws-samples/sample-claude-code-agent-team](https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-claude-code-agent-team), [github.com/revfactory/claude-code-harness](https://github.com/revfactory/claude-code-harness), [github.com/ruvnet/ruflo](https://github.com/ruvnet/ruflo)

### AWS Sample (most authoritative non-Anthropic source)

`aws-samples/sample-claude-code-agent-team`: Full Stack Developer parent orchestrating three specialists: Coding Agent, DevOps Agent, Review Agent. Uses spec-driven development, native agent teams feature.

### wshobson/agents (community marketplace)

84 plugins, 192 agents, 156 skills, 102 commands all defined as Markdown files. Cross-compatible with Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI. Uses the native `.claude/agents/` format.

### revfactory/harness (A/B tested)

Framework using architectural blueprints + role-based agent definitions + workflow orchestration via CLAUDE.md. Reported 60% quality improvement (49.5 → 79.3/100) in controlled experiment across 15 SE tasks. Uses CLAUDE.md as the primary orchestration layer.

### Anthropic's own blog post: dynamic workflows

Source: [claude.com/blog/a-harness-for-every-task-dynamic-workflows-in-claude-code](https://claude.com/blog/a-harness-for-every-task-dynamic-workflows-in-claude-code)

Anthropic uses the term "harness" to mean "the orchestration framework that coordinates agent execution." The key concept is **dynamic workflows** — Claude Opus 4.8+ can write its own orchestration harness (JavaScript) on the fly for each task rather than always using the static default. This is distinct from static CLAUDE.md-based orchestration. Dynamic workflows can: decide which models subagents use, run subagents in isolated worktrees, resume from checkpoints, process data programmatically.

---

## 9. Adversarial Verification: Claims That Need Correction

### Claim: "harness-builder invokes harness-evaluator"

**Partially incorrect.** If harness-builder runs as a subagent, it cannot spawn harness-evaluator (or any subagent). The main orchestrator session must invoke evaluator after builder returns. The pipeline in CLAUDE.md should direct the **orchestrator** to call both in sequence, not builder to call evaluator.

### Claim: Agent tool with `subagent_type` parameter

**Needs precision.** The `subagent_type` term appears in hooks documentation (as the value passed to `agent_type` matchers in SubagentStart/Stop hooks). When Claude invokes the Agent tool, it identifies the target subagent by its `name` field. The `--agents` CLI flag accepts a JSON object where keys are agent names. There is no separate "subagent_type" invocation parameter in the Agent tool itself — the routing is by name.

### Claim: `.claude/agents/` supports specifying provider (Claude vs. Gemini)

**Not supported via frontmatter.** The `model` field accepts model aliases and full Anthropic model IDs only (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, or `claude-*` IDs). Non-Anthropic models are not selectable via the `model` frontmatter field. Running Gemini models as subagents requires an MCP server or external tool bridge, not native frontmatter routing.

### Claim: CLAUDE.md orchestration is reliable for multi-step pipelines

**Conditionally true.** Works for soft routing if the file is concise. Fails for hard enforcement if the file is bloated. The official docs are explicit: long CLAUDE.md = ignored instructions. For a pipeline as complex as the Gidape harness, the instructions will compete with each other for attention.

---

## 10. Recommended Architecture for the Gidape Harness (Synthesis)

Based entirely on official documentation:

1. **Slim CLAUDE.md to <200 lines.** Use `@.harness/constitution.md`, `@.harness/memory-bank/product.md` etc. via import syntax. The routing table and pipeline description belong in imported files.

2. **`.claude/agents/` files for every subagent.** Currently working correctly. Descriptions are the routing mechanism — make them precise and include "use proactively when..." phrasing.

3. **Main session as orchestrator.** The orchestrator cannot be a subagent. The main Claude Code session invokes Agent tool → routes to subagents → receives summaries → chains to next agent. This matches the current design.

4. **Use hooks for deterministic gates.** Instead of CLAUDE.md instructions like "always run security-reviewer on auth files," configure a `SubagentStart` or `PostToolUse` hook in `.claude/settings.json` that fires based on file pattern.

5. **Agent Teams for true parallelism.** When builder and evaluator need to run concurrently and communicate, Agent Teams (experimental) is the correct feature. Today's sequential delegation (builder → evaluator) is correct for the non-experimental path.

6. **Subagent cannot call subagent.** Any spec that describes "harness-builder spawns harness-evaluator" must be revised: the orchestrator must chain them.

---

content.text:
A pesquisa revelou 3 problemas técnicos reais e específicos. Deixa eu ser direto.

---

## O que a pesquisa revelou — com fontes

### O harness no Claude Code FUNCIONA. Empresas fazem. Nós temos 3 erros concretos.

---

### Problema 1 — CRÍTICO: CLAUDE.md com 470 linhas (limite: 200)

**Fonte oficial:** [code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)

> *"Keep it concise. For each line, ask: 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?' If not, cut it. **Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!**"*
> 
> *Recommended: under 200 lines, under 2,000 tokens.*

**Nosso CLAUDE.md tem 470+ linhas.** Esta é a causa documentada de agentes não sendo chamados. Claude lê tudo, as instruções importantes se perdem no meio do contexto, e o instinto de "resolver direto" prevalece. **Não é falha de comportamento — é falha de arquitetura.**

A solução oficial é usar `@path/to/file` imports. O CLAUDE.md principal referencia arquivos detalhados, sem inliná-los.

---

### Problema 2 — ARQUITETURAL: Gemini não roda em `.claude/agents/`

**Fonte oficial:** [code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)

O campo `model` em `.claude/agents/` aceita **apenas model IDs da Anthropic**: `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, ou `claude-*`. Gemini não é suportado como subagent nativo.

Isso significa que `harness-frontend-builder` (Gemini Pro), `harness-doc-writer` (Gemini Flash), e `harness-memory-updater` (Gemini Flash Lite) **não podem ser chamados como subagentes**. Eles precisam ser invocados pelo orchestrator via script externo (`gemini-dispatch.sh`), não via Agent tool.

---

### Problema 3 — ARQUITETURAL: Subagents não podem spawnar outros subagents

**Fonte oficial:** [code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)

> *"Subagents cannot spawn other subagents. If your workflow requires nested delegation, use Skills or chain subagents from the main conversation."*

O Agent tool **não está disponível dentro de um subagent**. Isso quer dizer que se `harness-builder` tentar chamar `harness-evaluator`, vai falhar silenciosamente. **Somente o orchestrator (sessão principal) pode encadear agentes.** A cadeia `builder → evaluator → reviewer` deve ser orquestrada pela sessão principal, não pelos próprios agentes.

---

## O que fazem certo (empresas que funcionam)

**Fonte:** AWS Sample, revfactory/claude-code-harness, Anthropic blog:

| O que funciona | O que não funciona |
|---|---|
| CLAUDE.md conciso (<200 linhas) com `@imports` | CLAUDE.md longo com tudo inlined |
| Subagents com `description` precisa para auto-routing | Subagents com descriptions vagas |
| Orchestrator principal encadeia os agentes em sequência | Subagent tentando chamar outro subagent |
| Hooks em `settings.json` para enforcement determinístico | CLAUDE.md como único mecanismo de enforcement |
| Skills (`.claude/skills/`) para pipelines invocáveis | Confiar só em detecção de linguagem natural |

## Deep Research Report: Integrating Google Gemini into a Claude Code Harness (June 2026)

---

### Executive Summary

There are three production-grade patterns for calling Gemini from Claude Code, ranked by reliability and correctness: **(1) MCP server**, **(2) Gemini CLI subagent wrapper**, and **(3) Bash script direct API call**. The `gemini-dispatch.sh` Bash script pattern is functional but carries specific failure-mode risks. There is NO official Google-published MCP server for Gemini↔Claude Code integration — but several high-quality community servers exist. The `model:` field in Claude Code subagent YAML cannot natively route to Gemini — this is a confirmed Anthropic product limitation closed as "not planned."

### Q1: Does Google have an official MCP server for Gemini that Claude Code can use?

**Verdict: Partially. Google has an official Gemini API Docs MCP, but no official "call Gemini from Claude Code" server.**

Google publishes one official MCP endpoint: `https://gemini-api-docs-mcp.dev`, added via:
```bash
npx add-mcp "https://gemini-api-docs-mcp.dev"
```
This is a **documentation/search server** — it exposes a `search_documentation` tool so coding agents can look up Gemini API references in real time. It is **not** a server that lets Claude call Gemini as an AI model. Google's official docs page for coding agents ([ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/coding-agents](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/coding-agents)) explicitly lists Claude Code as a supported client for this docs MCP, but the capability is only "fetch Gemini API documentation," not "invoke Gemini as an LLM."

For actually invoking Gemini as an LLM from Claude Code, **all current solutions are community-built**, not official Google products. The best-maintained options:

| Repo | Stars | Auth | SDK or CLI | Production signals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [rlabs-inc/gemini-mcp](https://github.com/rlabs-inc/gemini-mcp) | 201 | API key | Gemini SDK | 37 tools, v0.7.2, OTel, 2,500+ tests |

| [ShunL12324/claude-code-gemini-mcp](https://github.com/ShunL12324/claude-code-gemini-mcp) | low | API key | OpenAI-compatible endpoint | Basic, early stage |
| [centminmod/gemini-cli-mcp-server](https://github.com/centminmod/gemini-cli-mcp-server) | active | Gemini CLI native auth | Wraps CLI via subprocess | 33 tools, enterprise-grade, Python/FastMCP |
| [DiversioTeam/gemini-cli-mcp](https://github.com/DiversioTeam/gemini-cli-mcp) | community | CLI auth | Wraps CLI | 4 tools, explicit "unofficial" disclaimer |

**`.claude/settings.json` configuration for the strongest option (rlabs-inc/gemini-mcp):**
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gemini": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/gemini-mcp/dist/index.js"],
      "env": {
        "GEMINI_API_KEY": "your-key-from-ai-studio",
        "GEMINI_PRO_MODEL": "gemini-2.5-pro",
        "GEMINI_FLASH_MODEL": "gemini-2.5-flash",
        "GEMINI_TOOL_PRESET": "text"

    }

}
```

For the Vertex AI variant (raydollete, production GCP):
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "gemini": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/gemini-for-claude-mcp/dist/app.js"],

        "GEMINI_DEFAULT_MODEL": "gemini-2.5-pro"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
(Requires `gcloud auth application-default login` and the principal having `roles/aiplatform.user`)

**Confidence: HIGH** — confirmed by multiple independent sources.

### Q2: Is the `gemini-dispatch.sh` Bash script approach reliable?

**Verdict: It works, but carries specific, documented failure modes.**

**How the Bash approach works:**
Claude Code's Bash tool spawns a subprocess, which runs `bash scripts/gemini-dispatch.sh "..."`. The script calls either `gemini -p "..."` (Gemini CLI) or `curl -X POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/...` (direct REST). Gemini responds after 5-60 seconds. Claude Code waits, receives stdout, continues.

**Confirmed failure modes:**

1. **2-minute default timeout / SIGTERM propagation bug** — The Bash tool default timeout is **120 seconds (2 minutes)**, hardcoded. A separate confirmed bug ([issue #45717](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/45717)) shows that when this timeout fires, the SIGTERM intended to kill the child process **propagates to the Claude Code parent process itself**, crashing the entire session (exit code 143). This is a regression present as of Claude Code 2.1.97 on Linux/tmux. Status: **open, not fixed as of June 2026**.

2. **Timeout configuration requires settings.json, not env vars** — The timeout can be extended in `~/.claude/settings.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "env": {
       "BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS": "300000",
       "BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS": "600000"
     }
   }
   ```
   Environment variable exports and shell wrappers (`gtimeout`, etc.) do NOT work — Claude Code uses a dual-layer internal timeout that overrides shell-level settings.

3. **Blocking nature** — A synchronous Bash call to an external AI is fully blocking. Claude Code waits with no partial progress. If the external AI is slow (e.g., Gemini 3-pro at high load), the agent appears frozen. There is no native streaming from Bash.

4. **No structured error surface** — If the script exits non-zero, Claude Code sees the stderr and exit code but has no structured way to distinguish "Gemini API rate limit" from "network timeout" from "bad API key."

**Workarounds for the dispatch.sh approach:**
- Pre-flight with a quick health check curl to the Gemini API before the full call
- Set `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` to 300000 (5 min) in settings.json
- Use the async hook pattern (see Q6) for fire-and-forget cases where you don't need the result inline
- Use `gemini -p "..." --output-format json` so output is parseable

**Is this what production teams do?** Some teams use it, but it's generally described as a workaround, not a canonical pattern. The Gemini CLI subagent wrapper (Pattern 2) and MCP bridge (Pattern 1) are considered cleaner.

---

### Q3: Custom MCP tool routing to Gemini internally ("gemini_design" pattern)

**Verdict: Yes, this is the canonical production pattern. Multiple production-grade implementations exist.**

The correct architecture is:
1. Claude Code has an MCP server registered (e.g., `gemini-cli-mcp` server)
2. Claude Code calls `gemini_prompt(text="Design a glassmorphism dashboard...")` as a tool call
3. The MCP server (Node.js or Python process) makes the Gemini API/SDK call internally
4. Returns structured result to Claude Code

This is **fully supported** by the MCP protocol. The MCP server handles all Gemini auth, retries, timeout management, and model selection — Claude Code just sees a tool that returns text. The centminmod/gemini-cli-mcp-server even has specific tools for UI-relevant tasks: `gemini_review_code`, `gemini_prompt`, `gemini_summarize`, and `gemini_ai_collaboration` which enables multi-turn design iteration.

For a UI generation use case specifically, the `rlabs-inc/gemini-mcp` server's **image generation tool** (via Gemini's multimodal capabilities) and **structured JSON output** tool are the most relevant.

---

### Q4: What successful teams actually do — concrete examples

**Pattern A: Gemini CLI subagent in Claude Code** (most documented pattern in 2026)

The [egghead.io tutorial](https://egghead.io/create-a-gemini-cli-powered-subagent-in-claude-code~adkge) and [wshobson/agents](https://github.com/wshobson/agents) repo document this pattern:

Create `.claude/agents/gemini-analyzer.md`:
```markdown
---
name: gemini-analyzer
description: Use when you need large-context codebase analysis (>100k tokens), second opinions on architecture, or UI generation. Delegates to Gemini via CLI.
tools: Bash, Read, Write
---
You are a wrapper for Gemini CLI. When given a task:
1. Run: gemini --all-files -p "[detailed prompt]"
2. Return the raw output without modification.
3. Use --yolo for non-destructive analysis tasks.
```

Claude Code's orchestrator then delegates to this subagent by description match. The subagent calls Gemini via `gemini -p "..."` in Bash. The result flows back to the orchestrator.

**Pattern B: MCP bridge** (cleaner, more production signals)

Teams with higher reliability requirements use one of the MCP servers listed in Q1. Tools are called explicitly: `@gemini query_gemini(prompt="...")` within Claude's tool-use loop.

**Pattern C: Bifrost proxy** (enterprise / full routing)

[Bifrost](https://www.getmaxim.ai/articles/how-to-use-claude-code-with-gemini-models-via-bifrost/) intercepts Claude Code's entire API call and routes it to Gemini. Set:
```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="gemini/gemini-2.5-pro"
```
Caveats: Claude-exclusive features (extended thinking, web search, computer use) don't work with Gemini behind this proxy. Tool use must be supported by the model. 11µs overhead per request.

**Pattern D: Multi-harness marketplace** (wshobson/agents)

The [wshobson/agents](https://github.com/wshobson/agents) repo provides a "multi-harness agentic plugin marketplace for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI" — enabling the same agent definitions to be portable across runtimes.

---

### Q5: The Gemini CLI — existence, installation, invocation

**Verdict: Yes, a fully-featured Gemini CLI exists, published and maintained by Google.**

- **Package**: `@google/gemini-cli` on npm
- **GitHub**: [google-gemini/gemini-cli](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli)
- **Official docs**: [geminicli.com/docs](https://geminicli.com/docs/)
- **Status**: Active, stable channel recommended for production, preview and nightly channels available

**Installation:**
```bash
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
# or one-shot without install:
npx @google/gemini-cli -p "your prompt"
```

**Non-interactive / bash scripting invocation:**
```bash
# Basic prompt, stdout response
GOOGLE_API_KEY=your-key gemini -p "Design a glassmorphism card component"

# With model selection
gemini -m gemini-2.5-pro -p "Design a UI layout"

# Structured JSON output (parseable in scripts)
gemini -p "..." --output-format json

# Streaming JSON (for real-time parsing)
gemini -p "..." --output-format stream-json

# With file context
gemini --all-files -p "Review this UI component"

# Skip confirmations (non-destructive use)
gemini --yolo -p "Analyze this codebase"
```

**Authentication for headless/automated use:**
```bash
# Option 1: API key (recommended for CI/scripts)
export GOOGLE_API_KEY="your-key-from-ai-studio"
gemini -p "..."

# Option 2: Service account (GCP)
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/service-account.json"
gemini -p "..."
```

Interactive OAuth is NOT available in headless mode — must use API key or service account.

**Exit codes:** 0=success, 1=general error, 42=input error, 53=turn limit exceeded.

### Q6: Timeout and blocking behavior in Claude Code's Bash tool

**Verified facts:**

| Fact | Source | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Default Bash timeout = 120 seconds | GitHub issue #5615 (confirmed by multiple users) | HIGH |
| SIGTERM propagation bug kills parent Claude Code process | GitHub issue #45717 (reproducible on Linux/tmux) | HIGH |
| `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` in settings.json env section DOES extend timeout | Issue #5615 verified workaround | MEDIUM (works for many, not all) |
| Shell-level `export BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=...` does NOT work | Issue #5615 confirmed not working | HIGH |
| Async hooks: marked `"async": true` in hooks config spawn background processes | Official Claude Code hooks docs | HIGH |
| Async hooks: Claude does NOT wait for async hook result | Official Claude Code hooks docs | HIGH |
| Async hooks: timeout still applies (hook killed at timeout, runs in background) | Official Claude Code hooks docs | HIGH |

**For long Gemini calls (30-60s) in the main Bash tool:**
- Extend the timeout via `~/.claude/settings.json` `env.BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`
- Be aware of the SIGTERM propagation bug on Linux — the call may crash Claude Code if it times out
- For Windows (your platform): the SIGTERM propagation bug may not apply since process groups work differently

**Async pattern for fire-and-forget Gemini calls (e.g., doc generation in hooks):**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "bash scripts/gemini-dispatch.sh",
        "async": true,
        "timeout": 120000
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```
With `async: true`, Claude Code does not block waiting for the Gemini response. This is the correct pattern for background doc generation (your Phase 4 Gemini doc sync).

### Q7: Is MCP the recommended pattern for non-Anthropic models in Claude Code?

**Verdict: Yes, MCP is the canonical recommended pattern. There is also an officially-recognized subagent+Bash wrapper pattern.**

From the official Claude Code subagents documentation: subagents have access to the `Bash` tool, which they can use to call external processes including the Gemini CLI. This is documented and explicitly used in the egghead.io tutorial. The subagent `model:` field, however, is **restricted to Anthropic model aliases** (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, or full Claude model IDs like `claude-sonnet-4-6`). Feature request #34821 to support non-Anthropic model IDs was **closed as "not planned"** by Anthropic.

This means: **Gemini cannot be the backing model of a Claude Code subagent natively.** But a subagent *backed by a Claude model* can call Gemini via Bash or MCP tools.

The two recommended patterns, ordered by production-grade-ness:

1. **MCP server** — Claude Code calls Gemini tools via MCP protocol. Structured, retryable, no timeout propagation risk, Claude sees typed tool responses. Best for interactive use where you need the result inline.

2. **Subagent + Bash wrapper** — A Claude subagent with `tools: Bash` calls `gemini -p "..."`. Simpler to set up, no MCP server to maintain. Works well for analysis tasks leveraging Gemini's 1M context window. Carries the Bash timeout risk.

**Confidence: HIGH** — confirmed by multiple independent sources.

---

### Q2: Is the `gemini-dispatch.sh` Bash script approach reliable?

**Verdict: It works, but carries specific, documented failure modes.**

**How the Bash approach works:**
Claude Code's Bash tool spawns a subprocess, which runs `bash scripts/gemini-dispatch.sh "..."`. The script calls either `gemini -p "..."` (Gemini CLI) or `curl -X POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/...` (direct REST). Gemini responds after 5-60 seconds. Claude Code waits, receives stdout, continues.

**Confirmed failure modes:**

1. **2-minute default timeout / SIGTERM propagation bug** — The Bash tool default timeout is **120 seconds (2 minutes)**, hardcoded. A separate confirmed bug ([issue #45717](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/45717)) shows that when this timeout fires, the SIGTERM intended to kill the child process **propagates to the Claude Code parent process itself**, crashing the entire session (exit code 143). This is a regression present as of Claude Code 2.1.97 on Linux/tmux. Status: **open, not fixed as of June 2026**.

2. **Timeout configuration requires settings.json, not env vars** — The timeout can be extended in `~/.claude/settings.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "env": {
       "BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS": "300000",
       "BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS": "600000"
     }
   }
   ```
   Environment variable exports and shell wrappers (`gtimeout`, etc.) do NOT work — Claude Code uses a dual-layer internal timeout that overrides shell-level settings.

3. **Blocking nature** — A synchronous Bash call to an external AI is fully blocking. Claude Code waits with no partial progress. If the external AI is slow (e.g., Gemini 3-pro at high load), the agent appears frozen. There is no native streaming from Bash.

4. **No structured error surface** — If the script exits non-zero, Claude Code sees the stderr and exit code but has no structured way to distinguish "Gemini API rate limit" from "network timeout" from "bad API key."

**Workarounds for the dispatch.sh approach:**
- Pre-flight with a quick health check curl to the Gemini API before the full call
- Set `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` to 300000 (5 min) in settings.json
- Use the async hook pattern (see Q6) for fire-and-forget cases where you don't need the result inline
- Use `gemini -p "..." --output-format json` so output is parseable

**Is this what production teams do?** Some teams use it, but it's generally described as a workaround, not a canonical pattern. The Gemini CLI subagent wrapper (Pattern 2) and MCP bridge (Pattern 1) are considered cleaner.

---

### Q3: Custom MCP tool routing to Gemini internally ("gemini_design" pattern)

**Verdict: Yes, this is the canonical production pattern. Multiple production-grade implementations exist.**

The correct architecture is:
1. Claude Code has an MCP server registered (e.g., `gemini-cli-mcp` server)
2. Claude Code calls `gemini_prompt(text="Design a glassmorphism dashboard...")` as a tool call
3. The MCP server (Node.js or Python process) makes the Gemini API/SDK call internally
4. Returns structured result to Claude Code

This is **fully supported** by the MCP protocol. The MCP server handles all Gemini auth, retries, timeout management, and model selection — Claude Code just sees a tool that returns text. The centminmod/gemini-cli-mcp-server even has specific tools for UI-relevant tasks: `gemini_review_code`, `gemini_prompt`, `gemini_summarize`, and `gemini_ai_collaboration` which enables multi-turn design iteration.

For a UI generation use case specifically, the `rlabs-inc/gemini-mcp` server's **image generation tool** (via Gemini's multimodal capabilities) and **structured JSON output** tool are the most relevant.

---

### Q4: What successful teams actually do — concrete examples

**Pattern A: Gemini CLI subagent in Claude Code** (most documented pattern in 2026)

The [egghead.io tutorial](https://egghead.io/create-a-gemini-cli-powered-subagent-in-claude-code~adkge) and [wshobson/agents](https://github.com/wshobson/agents) repo document this pattern:

Create `.claude/agents/gemini-analyzer.md`:
```markdown
---
name: gemini-analyzer
description: Use when you need large-context codebase analysis (>100k tokens), second opinions on architecture, or UI generation. Delegates to Gemini via CLI.
tools: Bash, Read, Write
---
You are a wrapper for Gemini CLI. When given a task:
1. Run: gemini --all-files -p "[detailed prompt]"
2. Return the raw output without modification.
3. Use --yolo for non-destructive analysis tasks.
```

Claude Code's orchestrator then delegates to this subagent by description match. The subagent calls Gemini via `gemini -p "..."` in Bash. The result flows back to the orchestrator.

**Pattern B: MCP bridge** (cleaner, more production signals)

Teams with higher reliability requirements use one of the MCP servers listed in Q1. Tools are called explicitly: `@gemini query_gemini(prompt="...")` within Claude's tool-use loop.

**Pattern C: Bifrost proxy** (enterprise / full routing)

[Bifrost](https://www.getmaxim.ai/articles/how-to-use-claude-code-with-gemini-models-via-bifrost/) intercepts Claude Code's entire API call and routes it to Gemini. Set:
```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080/anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL="gemini/gemini-2.5-pro"
```
Caveats: Claude-exclusive features (extended thinking, web search, computer use) don't work with Gemini behind this proxy. Tool use must be supported by the model. 11µs overhead per request.

**Pattern D: Multi-harness marketplace** (wshobson/agents)

The [wshobson/agents](https://github.com/wshobson/agents) repo provides a "multi-harness agentic plugin marketplace for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI" — enabling the same agent definitions to be portable across runtimes.

---

### Q5: The Gemini CLI — existence, installation, invocation

**Verdict: Yes, a fully-featured Gemini CLI exists, published and maintained by Google.**

- **Package**: `@google/gemini-cli` on npm
- **GitHub**: [google-gemini/gemini-cli](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli)
- **Official docs**: [geminicli.com/docs](https://geminicli.com/docs/)
- **Status**: Active, stable channel recommended for production, preview and nightly channels available

**Installation:**
```bash
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli
# or one-shot without install:
npx @google/gemini-cli -p "your prompt"
```

**Non-interactive / bash scripting invocation:**
```bash
# Basic prompt, stdout response
GOOGLE_API_KEY=your-key gemini -p "Design a glassmorphism card component"

# With model selection
gemini -m gemini-2.5-pro -p "Design a UI layout"

# Structured JSON output (parseable in scripts)
gemini -p "..." --output-format json

# Streaming JSON (for real-time parsing)
gemini -p "..." --output-format stream-json

# With file context
gemini --all-files -p "Review this UI component"

# Skip confirmations (non-destructive use)
gemini --yolo -p "Analyze this codebase"
```

**Authentication for headless/automated use:**
```bash
# Option 1: API key (recommended for CI/scripts)
export GOOGLE_API_KEY="your-key-from-ai-studio"
gemini -p "..."

# Option 2: Service account (GCP)
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/service-account.json"
gemini -p "..."
```

Interactive OAuth is NOT available in headless mode — must use API key or service account.

**Exit codes:** 0=success, 1=general error, 42=input error, 53=turn limit exceeded.

---

### Q6: Timeout and blocking behavior in Claude Code's Bash tool

**Verified facts:**

| Fact | Source | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Default Bash timeout = 120 seconds | GitHub issue #5615 (confirmed by multiple users) | HIGH |
| SIGTERM propagation bug kills parent Claude Code process | GitHub issue #45717 (reproducible on Linux/tmux) | HIGH |
| `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` in settings.json env section DOES extend timeout | Issue #5615 verified workaround | MEDIUM (works for many, not all) |
| Shell-level `export BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=...` does NOT work | Issue #5615 confirmed not working | HIGH |
| Async hooks: marked `"async": true` in hooks config spawn background processes | Official Claude Code hooks docs | HIGH |
| Async hooks: Claude does NOT wait for async hook result | Official Claude Code hooks docs | HIGH |
| Async hooks: timeout still applies (hook killed at timeout, runs in background) | Official Claude Code hooks docs | HIGH |

**For long Gemini calls (30-60s) in the main Bash tool:**
- Extend the timeout via `~/.claude/settings.json` `env.BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`
- Be aware of the SIGTERM propagation bug on Linux — the call may crash Claude Code if it times out
- For Windows (your platform): the SIGTERM propagation bug may not apply since process groups work differently

**Async pattern for fire-and-forget Gemini calls (e.g., doc generation in hooks):**
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "command",
        "command": "bash scripts/gemini-dispatch.sh",
        "async": true,
        "timeout": 120000
      }]
    }]
  }
}
```
With `async: true`, Claude Code does not block waiting for the Gemini response. This is the correct pattern for background doc generation (your Phase 4 Gemini doc sync).

---

### Q7: Is MCP the recommended pattern for non-Anthropic models in Claude Code?

**Verdict: Yes, MCP is the canonical recommended pattern. There is also an officially-recognized subagent+Bash wrapper pattern.**

From the official Claude Code subagents documentation: subagents have access to the `Bash` tool, which they can use to call external processes including the Gemini CLI. This is documented and explicitly used in the egghead.io tutorial. The subagent `model:` field, however, is **restricted to Anthropic model aliases** (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, or full Claude model IDs like `claude-sonnet-4-6`). Feature request #34821 to support non-Anthropic model IDs was **closed as "not planned"** by Anthropic.

This means: **Gemini cannot be the backing model of a Claude Code subagent natively.** But a subagent *backed by a Claude model* can call Gemini via Bash or MCP tools.

The two recommended patterns, ordered by production-grade-ness:

1. **MCP server** — Claude Code calls Gemini tools via MCP protocol. Structured, retryable, no timeout propagation risk, Claude sees typed tool responses. Best for interactive use where you need the result inline.

2. **Subagent + Bash wrapper** — A Claude subagent with `tools: Bash` calls `gemini -p "..."`. Simpler to set up, no MCP server to maintain. Works well for analysis tasks leveraging Gemini's 1M context window. Carries the Bash timeout risk.

---

### Q8: Is `gemini-dispatch.sh` what production teams use, or is it a hack?

**Verdict: It's a pragmatic workaround, not a hack per se, but it has real production risks. MCP is the cleaner path.**

Evidence for "it's used in production":
- The Google-official [google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli](https://github.com/google-github-actions/run-gemini-cli) GitHub Action wraps Gemini CLI as a shell dispatch — Google itself ships this pattern for CI/CD automation
- The DeepLearning.AI [sc-gemini-cli-files dispatch workflow](https://deepwiki.com/https-deeplearning-ai/sc-gemini-cli-files/6.1-dispatch-workflow-and-event-routing) is a production GitHub workflow using Gemini via bash dispatch
- Multiple teams (testinginproduction.co, inventivehq.com) document bash-driven Gemini invocation for automation

Evidence for "it has real risks in Claude Code specifically":
- The 2-minute timeout with SIGTERM propagation bug is a live regression in the Claude Code Bash tool
- No structured error surface (API errors look like generic failures)
- Blocking: no partial results during long Gemini calls
- For the specific use case in your CLAUDE.md (Phase 4 doc sync before push), async hooks is the correct pattern — not inline Bash

**For your specific `harness-doc-writer` Gemini call pattern:**

The right architecture in your project is:
1. **Interactive tasks** (Gemini Pro for UI design, invoked by harness-frontend-builder subagent): Use an MCP server. Register `rlabs-inc/gemini-mcp` or `raydollete/gemini-for-claude-mcp` in `.claude/settings.json`. The subagent calls `query_gemini(...)` as a tool, not a Bash subprocess.

2. **Background tasks** (Phase 4 doc sync, the current `gemini-dispatch.sh` pattern): Convert to an **async Claude Code hook** with `"async": true`. This removes the blocking risk entirely. The doc generation runs in background after the commit, does not block the push.

3. **Large-context analysis** (reviewing full codebases with Gemini's 1M window): Use the subagent+Bash wrapper pattern (`gemini --all-files -p "..."`) — this is explicitly documented and produces clean results.

---
name: harness-doc-writer
description: Escritor de documentação do MommaERP. Lê o diff do que foi implementado e atualiza diretamente as docs de usuário em docs/ (MkDocs), CHANGELOG.md. Invocado na Phase 4 antes do push. Escreve exclusivamente em pt-BR. Use quando: sincronizar docs de usuário após feature implementada, atualizar CHANGELOG.
model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
tools:
  - Read
  - Write
  - Edit
  - Glob
  - Grep
  - Bash
---

Você é **harness-doc-writer**, responsável por sincronizar a documentação de usuário do MommaERP após cada feature. Você lê o diff, entende o que mudou, e edita os arquivos `.md` diretamente. Escreve exclusivamente em **pt-BR**.

**Regra fundamental:** Documenta SOMENTE o que o diff confirma foi implementado. Nunca inventa funcionalidade.

---

## Critério: mudança visível ao usuário?

Antes de atualizar qualquer doc, classificar o diff:

```
VISÍVEL AO USUÁRIO → documentar:
✅ Novo campo em formulário
✅ Nova ação/botão disponível
✅ Comportamento mudou (validação, ordem, fluxo)
✅ Nova página ou aba adicionada
✅ Mensagem de erro ou toast mudou

INTERNO → NÃO documentar:
❌ Refactor (mesmo comportamento, código diferente)
❌ Otimização de query/performance sem mudança de UX
❌ Adição de teste sem mudança de comportamento
❌ Renomeação de variável/arquivo sem impacto na UI
```

Dúvida? Perguntar: **"Um operador de loja notaria a diferença?"** Se não → não documentar.

---

## Estrutura de docs (publicada em momma-xi.vercel.app/docs)

```
docs/
├── guia-rapido/
├── modulos/
│   ├── estoque/        ← src/features/estoque/, compras/
│   ├── financeiro/     ← src/features/financeiro/
│   ├── logistica/      ← src/features/logistica/, requisicoes/
│   ├── producao/       ← src/features/producao/
│   └── funcionarios/   ← src/features/funcionarios/
├── ferramentas/        ← etiquetas, scanner, rastreabilidade
├── inteligencia-artificial/ ← src/features/mia/
├── administracao/      ← src/features/admin/, usuarios/
└── faq/                ← glossário, atalhos
```

**NUNCA editar:**
- `docs/mia/` — arquitetura interna
- `docs/arquitetura/` — ADRs
- `docs/qa-security-review/`

---

## Padrão das páginas (Material MkDocs)

```markdown
---
description: Descrição curta para SEO (1 linha)
---

# 📋 Título da Página

Parágrafo introdutório.

---

## ✨ Funcionalidades principais

- **Feature 1**: descrição

---

## 📖 Como usar

### Passo 1: Título

Explicação do passo.

!!! tip "Dica"
    Informação útil.

!!! warning "Atenção"
    Algo importante.
```

Regras: headings com emoji · admonitions Material · tabelas para comparações · `---` como separador · linguagem simples para operador de loja.

---

## Mapeamento feature → docs

| Feature tocada | Atualizar em |
|---|---|
| `src/features/estoque/` | `docs/modulos/estoque/` |
| `src/features/compras/` | `docs/modulos/estoque/compras.md` |
| `src/features/financeiro/` | `docs/modulos/financeiro/` |
| `src/features/mia/` | `docs/inteligencia-artificial/mia-chat.md` |
| `src/features/admin/` | `docs/administracao/` |
| `src/features/funcionarios/` | `docs/administracao/funcionarios.md` |
| nova ferramenta (scanner, etiquetas) | `docs/ferramentas/` |
| novo termo de negócio | `docs/faq/glossario.md` |

---

## CHANGELOG.md — formato Keep a Changelog

```markdown
## [Não lançado]

### Adicionado
- Nova funcionalidade X (feat)

### Corrigido
- Bug Y corrigido (fix)

### Alterado
- Comportamento Z ajustado (refactor/chore)
```

Bullets ≤80 chars · pt-BR · sem referência a Claude/IA.

---

## Rebuild obrigatório

```bash
npm run docs:build   # gera public/docs/ servido pelo Vite
```

Verificar que build passa sem erro antes de reportar conclusão.

---

## O que você NÃO faz
- Não edita docs excluídas do site
- Não inventa funcionalidade — só documenta o que está no diff
- Não escreve em inglês
- Não atualiza memory-bank do harness (papel do harness-memory-updater)

# CLAUDE.md — Gidape
> ERP interno Momma (doces saudáveis, multi-loja, Brasília). Standalone.
> Contexto: @.harness/memory-bank/product.md · @.harness/memory-bank/architecture.md

---

## ⚡ PROTOCOLO — EXECUTAR ANTES DE QUALQUER AÇÃO

Para toda mensagem que envolve código, percorrer esta árvore **antes** de agir:

```
Envolve UI / visual / className / layout / componente React?
  SIM → Agent(harness-frontend-builder)  ← chama Gemini Pro internamente via Bash
         → Agent(harness-builder)         ← implementa o design retornado
  NÃO ↓

Implementa código (feature / fix / hook / migration)?
  SIM → Pipeline Fase 0-5. Agent(harness-builder) implementa.
  NÃO ↓

Investiga causa de bug (root-cause não claro)?
  SIM → Agent(harness-debugger) → RCA → builder depois
  NÃO ↓

Revisa código já implementado?
  SIM → Agent(harness-frontend-reviewer) ∥ Agent(harness-security-reviewer) → Agent(harness-evaluator)
  NÃO ↓

É leitura / pergunta / carve-out (≤3 linhas + 1 arquivo + sem UI + mecânico)?
  SIM → Resposta direta ou edição direta
  NÃO → Voltou ao topo. Escolher o branch correto.
```

**Antes de cada ação declarar em texto: `🔧 [agente ou Bash(Gemini)] — [motivo]`**
Sem declaração = sem harness = errado.

**Proibido sem exceção:**
- Editar `.tsx` com visual sem Gemini (design) + harness-builder (código)
- Implementar sem branch isolada + pipeline completo
- Auto-avaliar próprio código (evaluator existe para isso)
- Push sem Phase 3.5 + 3.6 completos

---

## AGENTES

### Claude — via `Agent` tool (subagent_type = nome abaixo)

| Nome | Modelo | Quando |
|---|---|---|
| `harness-builder` | sonnet-4-6 | Toda implementação (feat/fix/refactor) — TDD-first |
| `harness-evaluator` | opus-4-7 | QA após builder — nunca self-eval |
| `harness-architect` | opus-4-7 | Migration SQL (gate obrigatório) + decisão arq. |
| `harness-debugger` | opus-4-7 | Root-cause de bug não óbvio |
| `harness-planner` | opus-4-7 | Features L/XL — expande spec em PRD |
| `harness-clarifier` | sonnet-4-6 | Spec ambígua → spec.md estruturada |
| `harness-frontend-reviewer` | sonnet-4-6 | Revisão UI pós-build (paralelo) |
| `harness-security-reviewer` | sonnet-4-6 | RLS/auth/PII (condicional por arquivo) |

System prompts: `.claude/agents/<nome>.md`

### Agentes de suporte (Claude Haiku — leves e diretos)

| Nome | Modelo | Quando |
|---|---|---|
| `harness-doc-writer` | haiku | Docs de usuário + CHANGELOG (Phase 4) |
| `harness-memory-updater` | haiku | Atualiza memory-bank pós-feature (Phase 3.7) |

> **Nota sobre Gemini:** `harness-frontend-builder` é um Claude Sonnet subagent que chama Gemini Pro
> internamente via `bash scripts/gemini-dispatch.sh` — este é o padrão correto documentado pelo
> egghead.io e Anthropic. O orchestrator invoca `Agent(harness-frontend-builder)` normalmente;
> o subagent gerencia a chamada Gemini por conta própria. Timeout configurado para 5min em settings.json.

---

| Sinal | Tipo | Ação imediata |
|---|---|---|
| "feat", "implementar", "adicionar", "criar", "nova feature" | feature | Pipeline feat |
| "fix", "corrigir", "bug", "não funciona", "quebrou", "tá errado" | fix | Pipeline fix (3 perguntas obrigatórias) |
| "refatorar", "simplificar", "extrair", "limpar" | refactor | Playbook refactor |
| "aperfeiçoar", "melhorar", "otimizar", "polir" | feat ou refactor | 1 pergunta: novo comportamento? |
| "investigar", "analisar", "por que", "o que causa" | Tier 0+ | harness-debugger se RCA |
| "revisar", "revisa", "olha esse código" | Tier 0+ | reviewer + evaluator direto |
| Mudança >3 linhas ou >1 arquivo | catch-all | Inferir tipo acima |

Você é **harness-frontend-builder**, o especialista em design de UI do MommaERP (Gidape).

## Como você funciona

Você é um Claude Sonnet subagent que **chama Gemini Pro via Bash** para gerar designs. O padrão é:

1. Recebe a tarefa de design do orchestrator (spec.md ou descrição direta)
2. Constrói um prompt de design rico com contexto do MommaERP
3. Chama Gemini Pro via `bash scripts/gemini-dispatch.sh`
4. Recebe o design output do Gemini
5. Escreve `design.md` em `.harness/spec/<slug>/design.md`
6. Cria scaffold do componente em `src/features/<nome>/ui/<Nome>.page.tsx`

## Invocar Gemini Pro

```bash
# Construir o prompt com contexto completo e chamar o script
MODEL=gemini-3.1-pro-preview bash scripts/gemini-dispatch.sh <<'PROMPT'
Você é um especialista em design de UI para o MommaERP (Gidape) — ERP de uma confeitaria artesanal saudável (Momma) em Brasília, Brasil. React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind.

DESIGN SYSTEM OBRIGATÓRIO — glassmorphism verde:
- Cor da marca: #57715B (sage verde)
- Wrapper de página: MommaPageLayout (stripe verde automático no topo)
- Cards: bg-white/40 backdrop-blur-md border border-white/20 rounded-2xl shadow-sm
- KPI cards: bg-white/60 dark:bg-[#1A1A1A]/60 rounded-[2rem] p-6 + watermark ícone
- Botão primário: bg-[#57715B] hover:bg-[#465b49] text-white
- Tipografia: Poppins; números = tabular-nums
- PROIBIDO: bege, marrom, pie/donut charts, larguras fixas de viewport
- Mobile-first: 375px primeiro, breakpoints md: lg: depois

TAREFA DE DESIGN:
[INSERIR DESCRIÇÃO DA TAREFA AQUI]

OUTPUT ESPERADO:
1. Estrutura visual descrita em markdown
2. JSX completo com as classes Tailwind corretas
3. Responsividade documentada (mobile → desktop)
4. Estados: loading (skeleton), vazio (empty state), erro
PROMPT
```

**Substituir `[INSERIR DESCRIÇÃO DA TAREFA AQUI]` pelo pedido específico do orchestrator.**

## Identidade visual (contexto para o prompt Gemini)

```
Glassmorphism verde sage #57715B sobre fundo branco
Componentes: MommaPageLayout, GlassCard, KPI cards com watermark
Proibido: bege, marrom, pie/donut/gauge, larguras fixas
Mobile-first obrigatório: maioria opera em celular
Dark mode: toda cor precisa variante dark:
```

### Tipos de página

**Dashboard/Overview:**
- KPIs grid (1 col mobile → 2-3 desktop)
- Sem charts de pizza — barras ou números
- Tabela de itens recentes abaixo dos KPIs

**Lista com ações:**
- Header com título + botão primário
- Tabela com overflow-x-auto
- Sheet (lateral) para formulários

**Formulário/Modal:**
- Sheet lateral para formulários relacionados
- Dialog para confirmações destrutivas
- Botões rodapé: Cancelar (ghost) + Salvar (bg-[#57715B])

## Output obrigatório

Após receber a resposta do Gemini, salvar em dois lugares:

**1. `.harness/spec/<slug>/design.md`:**
```markdown
# Design — <nome>

## Estrutura visual
<descrição do layout>

## Componentes usados
- MommaPageLayout
- GlassCard
- ...

## Responsividade
- Mobile (375px): ...
- Desktop: ...

## Estados
- Loading: skeleton pulse
- Vazio: empty state com ícone + CTA
- Erro: badge vermelho + retry

## JSX principal
<jsx gerado pelo Gemini>
```

**2. Scaffold em `src/features/<nome>/ui/<Nome>.page.tsx`:**
```tsx
import { MommaPageLayout } from '@/shared/components/layout/MommaPageLayout'
// imports adicionais

export default function <Nome>Page() {
  return (
    <MommaPageLayout>
      {/* estrutura do design — para o builder preencher */}
    </MommaPageLayout>
  )
}
```

## Se Gemini falhar

Se o script retornar erro ou timeout:
```bash
# Verificar se gemini-dispatch.sh existe e a chave está configurada
cat scripts/gemini-dispatch.sh | head -5
# Tentar com modelo mais rápido
MODEL=gemini-3-flash bash scripts/gemini-dispatch.sh "..."
```

Se continuar falhando, gerar o design diretamente com base no design system documentado acima — não bloquear o orchestrator.
